newsitem.title: ITALY: Uproar over envoy to Albania embarrasses Italy.
newsitem.headline: Uproar over envoy to Albania embarrasses Italy.

text.p: Italy faced embarrassment on Sunday over its role in Albania on the eve of an international meeting that is meant to boost efforts to haul the Balkan state back to law and order and smooth the path to democratic elections.

With senior diplomats heading to Rome for Monday's talks, newspaper reports said the Italian ambassador to Tirana Paolo Foresti would be replaced following allegations that he was biased in favour of Albania's embattled President Sali Berisha.

The allegations, denied by Foresti, were made last week by the Albanian opposition newspaper Indipendent which carried a purported transcript of a telephone conversation between Foresti and the chairman of Berisha's Democratic Party, Tritan Shehu.

In the published exchange, which Foresti says is fabricated, the envoy appears to try to undermine the role of European mediator Franz Vranitzky and to offer to help broker a deal with the Albanian opposition in Berisha's favour.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini has noted Foresti's denials and stated publicly that the purported remarks "do not correspond to the Italian government's position".
His ministry declined on Sunday to comment in detail on the reports, which said the envoy would be succeeded shortly by Manfredo Incisa di Camerana, a former ambassador to Mozambique.
Diplomatic sources said the situation was being examined and that any decision would be taken by the cabinet.
"The search is for a person of a sufficiently high profile to manage the situation in Albania," one source said.

Italy, with strong trade ties to Albania and eager to stem an influx of illegal immigrants from across the Adriatic, has played an active part in international attempts to brake the impoverished state's slide into anarchy.

It leads a multinational military force deployed in Albania following rioting and looting in February and March after anger at the collapse of shady investment schemes mushroomed into an uprising against Berisha in the south of the country.

Dini championed the installation in March of a nine-party national unity government led by opposition Socialist Bashkim Fino under an accord designed to lead to early parliamentary elections on June 29.

Diplomatic sources said Monday's meeting was expected to end with a declaration of strong support for the electoral process and a signal to Albania's squabbling political parties to ensure the ballot can go ahead in a climate of calm.
Dini, Fino and Vranitzky, the Albania envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), will all take part in the talks.

Other participants include Washington's Balkans troubleshooter, John Kornblum, and officials from European Union countries and a host of international organisations including the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

The day-long talks, which will include a review of the work so far of the multinational security mission, are intended to pave the way for a full ministerial conference on Albania, tentatively scheduled to take place in Rome on June 18.
Foresti told the Italian news agency ANSA in Tirana that he would not attend Monday's meeting. "I am waiting for the government to tell me I can pack my bags," he said.

Foresti's assignment was to have ended last December but his move was frozen when Albania plunged into crisis. Newspaper reports said controversy over his purported pro-Berisha stance had accelerated steps to replace him.
